facts.statement: Ahshislepelta was named in 2011 by paleontologists Michael Burns and Robert M. Sullivan.
facts.quote: It was named in 2011 by Michael Burns and Robert M. Sullivan.

facts.statement: A partial skeleton of Ahshislepelta was discovered in 2005 at the Ah-shi-sle-pah Wilderness Study Area in New Mexico.
facts.quote: In 2005, a partial postcranial skeleton of an ankylosaur was discovered from the Hunter Wash Member in the lower part of the Kirtland Formation, New Mexico at the Ah-shi-sle-pah Wilderness Study Area.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was collected during field seasons between 2005 and 2009 before being formally described in 2011.
facts.quote: The specimen was later collected over consecutive field seasons from 2005 to 2009 and was subsequently described in 2011 by Michael Burns and Robert M. Sullivan.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen (SMP VP-1930) includes a partial girdle, vertebrae fragments, thoracic osteoderms, and other postcranial parts.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, SMP VP-1930, consists of a partial girdle, partial scapulocoracoid, a proximal portion of the radius, numerous cervical and/or dorsal vertebrae fragments, complete and fragmentary thoracic osteoderms, and other unidentifiable postcranial fragments.

facts.statement: Ahshislepelta lived during the Late Cretaceous (74.5 million years ago) in the Hunter Wash Member of the Kirtland Formation in New Mexico.
facts.quote: Ahshislepelta (meaning "Ah-shi-sle-pah Wash shield") is a monospecific genus of ankylosaur dinosaur from New Mexico that lived during the Late Cretaceous (late Campanian stage, 74.5 Ma) in what is now the Hunter Wash Member of the Kirtland Formation.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests the environment where Ahshislepelta lived had a warm temperate to subtropical climate.
facts.quote: Based on the abundance of angiosperms with leaves that have entire or nearly entire margins and drip points, the Kirtland Formation may have had a warm temperate to subtropical climate.

facts.statement: Ahshislepelta coexisted with Stegoceras, Navajoceratops, Terminocavus, Ziapelta, Bistahieversor, and Navajodactylus.
facts.quote: Ahshislepelta coexisted with the pachycephalosaurid Stegoceras, the chasmosaurine ceratopsids Navajoceratops and Terminocavus, the ankylosaurine ankylosaurid Ziapelta, the eutyrannosaur tyrannosauroid Bistahieversor, and the azhdarchid pterosaur Navajodactylus.

facts.statement: Based on humerus size, Ahshislepelta was larger than Eopinacosaurus but smaller than Talarurus and Pinacosaurus grangeri.
facts.quote: Based on the size of the humerus, Ahshislepelta is larger than Eopinacosaurus mephistocephalus but smaller than Talarurus and Pinacosaurus grangeri.

facts.statement: The genus name Ahshislepelta combines the locality name Ah-shi-sle-pah Wash with the Greek word for shield, peltè.
facts.quote: The generic name, Ahshislepelta, is derived from Ah-shi-sle-pah Wash, the locality from which the holotype came, and the Ancient Greek word "peltè" (shield).

facts.statement: The species name minor refers to its small adult size compared to other North American ankylosaurids.
facts.quote: The specific name, minor, is in reference to its small adult size relative to other North American ankylosaurids.

facts.statement: Ahshislepelta is distinguished by a scapular acromion process that overhangs to 25% of the scapula's dorsoventral width.
facts.quote: Burns & Sullivan (2011) diagnosed Ahshislepelta based on the dorsolateral overhang of the scapular acromion process to 25% of the dorsoventral width of the scapula.

facts.statement: Unlike other ankylosaurids except Euoplocephalus, Ahshislepelta has osteoderms with uniformly pitted texture and sparse neurovascular grooves.
facts.quote: Ahshislepelta differs from other ankylosaurids, with the exception of Euoplocephalus, by the superficial osteodermal surface texture, characterized by uniformly distributed pitted rugosity, and sparse distribution of reticular neurovascular grooves with neurovascular foramina extending perpendicularly to obliquely into the bone.

facts.statement: The coracoid bone is approximately 16 cm long with the foramen located anterodorsal to the glenoid cavity.
facts.quote: The coracoid is roughly 16 cm long and the coracoid foramen is anterodorsal to the glenoid cavity.

facts.statement: The left humerus is massive and measures 31 cm in length.
facts.quote: As in ankylosaurids, the left humerus is massive and has a length of 31 cm.

facts.statement: The well-developed deltopectoral crest on the left humerus measures 15 cm at its widest point.
facts.quote: The left humerus preserves a deltopectoral crest that is well-developed and measures 15 cm across the widest portion of the humerus.

facts.statement: The largest osteoderm, located in the thoracic region, measures 15 cm long, 12 cm wide, and 10 cm high.
facts.quote: The largest osteoderm pertains to the thoracic region behind the cervical region based on the similar morphology to the median thoracic osteoderms of the holotype specimen of Scolosaurus. The osteoderm has a length of 15 cm, a width of 12 cm and a height of 10 cm.

facts.statement: The smallest associated ossicle has a diameter of 1 cm.
facts.quote: The smallest ossicle has a diameter of 1 cm.

facts.statement: Burns and Sullivan originally classified Ahshislepelta as an ankylosaurid within Ankylosaurinae, though this was not based on phylogenetic analysis.
facts.quote: Burns & Sullivan (2011) originally placed Ahshislepelta as an ankylosaurid within the clade Ankylosaurinae, although this was not based on the result of a phylogenetic analysis.

facts.statement: Several studies have favored classifying Ahshislepelta as a nodosaurid rather than an ankylosaurid.
facts.quote: On the other hand, several other studies have favored a nodosaurid position.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Ahshislepelta belongs to Ankylosauridae or Nodosauridae, with some analyses supporting Ankylosauridae and others supporting Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: Arbour & Currie (2015) favors an ankylosaurid position. Their results are reproduced below.

facts.statement: The fossils were discovered in 2005 and collected between 2005 and 2009 from the Hunter Wash Member of the Kirtland Formation in the San Juan Basin of New Mexico, USA.
facts.quote: Fue descubierto en 2005 y recolectado entre 2005 y 2009 en el Miembro Hunter Wash de la formación Kirtland en la localidad de Ah-shi-sle-pah Wash, descubierto en los depósitos de la Cuenca San Juan, en Nuevo México, Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: The genus was named by Michael E. Burns and Robert M. Sullivan in 2011, with the type species being Ahshislepelta minor.
facts.quote: Ahshislepelta fue nombrado por Michael E. Burns y Robert M. Sullivan en el año de 2011 y la especie tipo es Ahshislepelta minor.

facts.statement: Researchers identified a unique derived feature: a projection on the scapula where the acromial process forms an overhang equal to one-quarter of the scapula's width.
facts.quote: Los descriptores fueron capaces de establecer una característica derivada únicas, una protuberancia en el omóplato, el proceso acromial forma un voladizo que es la cuarta parte de la anchura de la escápula.

facts.statement: The scapula and coracoid were firmly fused into an escapulocoracoid, indicating that the specimen was not a juvenile.
facts.quote: La escápula y el coracoides están firmemente fundidos en un escapulocoracoides, una señal de que no es un animal joven.

facts.statement: Many bone plates were known from the left scapular region; the largest were circular or curved-ridged with a hollow crescent-shaped bottom, while smaller ones had higher ridges and an oval shape.
facts.quote: Hay un gran número de placas de hueso se conoce, de la zona de la escápula izquierda. Los más grandes son circulares o con una quilla curvada y una parte inferior hueco en forma de media luna, de modo que el espesor no es grande, los más pequeños tienen una quilla más alta y son más de forma oval.

facts.statement: Unlike other ankylosaurs, Ahshislepelta osteoderms had a rough surface formed by uniformly spaced pits carved by a network of widely separated grooves positioned in front of veins and nerves.
facts.quote: Los de Ahshislepelta, sin embargo, son de forma similar a los de Euoplocephalus, la superficie rugosa se forma por medio de pozos espaciados uniformemente, surcada por una red de ranuras muy separados que se colocan delante de las venas y nervios, en el que las aberturas para ello taza de pie sobre la superficie del hueso.

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Ahshislepelta is Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ankylosauridae

facts.statement: Ahshislepelta belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: The time range for the genus Ahshislepelta is from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus is known from the holotype SMP VP-1930, an associated but incomplete postcranial skeleton of an adult consisting of a shoulder girdle, partial left forelimb, vertebrae, and osteoderms.
facts.quote: Ahshislepelta es conocido a partir del holotipo SMP VP-1930, un esqueleto postcraneal asociado e incompleto de un individuo adulto que consiste en una cintura escapular, un miembro delantero izquierdo parcial, vértebras y osteodermos.

facts.statement: The scientific name derives from the locality Ah-shi-sle-pah Wash where the fossils were found and the Greek word pelta, meaning "shield".
facts.quote: El nombre científico viene de la localidad de Ah-shi-sle-pah Wash en donde sus fósiles se hallaron, y pelta, término griego para "escudo".

facts.statement: The species name minor comes from Latin, meaning "small," referring to its adult size being smaller than other North American ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie se deriva del latín minor, "pequeño" en referencia a su tamaño adulto que es menor comparado al de otros anquilosáuridos de Norteamérica.
